articles.title: Muru
articles.summary_raw: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 2026-11-05 — A first look at Muru 2026-11-07 — Muru: looking inside the workers 2026-11-08 — Muru: how it fits together 2026-11-09 — Muru: import once, fork many 2026-11-10 — Muru: HTTPS in development 2026-11-11 — Muru: WSGI and ASGI together 2026-11-11 — AI as a lifestyle choice 2026-11-12 — Muru: releases, not restarts 2026-11-13 — Muru: canaries without a service mesh 2026-11-14 — Muru: a better tenant in a container 2026-11-15 — Muru: working with Kubernetes, not around it 2026-11-16 — Muru: scaling from what the workers report 2026-11-17 — Muru: scaling to zero 2026-11-18 — Muru: overlays on a schedule 2026-11-19 — Muru: noticing and responding 2026-11-20 — Muru: a toolbar on every page 2026-11-21 — Muru: tracing in the toolbar That post about AI as a lifestyle choice is particularly worth a read: The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me, and twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi turns out to be useful for that. I am prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something I would trust, and something you would too. Tags: graham-dumpleton , modwsgi , python , wsgi , ai , rust , asgi , generative-ai , llms , ai-assisted-programming

articles.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
articles.summary_raw: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. [...] Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line. — Levent Alpöge , alpo.ge/remark.pdf Tags: anthropic , claude , generative-ai , mathematics , ai , llms , levent-alpoge
